description: Rules every generated Vanguard attack row must satisfy. Every entry in `rules` is sourced from the Game Design Document itself, not from measured implementation values -- that separation is deliberate. Schema mechanics live in `contract` below and are enforced by the deterministic gate; the GDD rules are what the evaluator scores.

status_legend.GDD: Stated in the GDD. The evaluator enforces it as a requirement.
status_legend.OPEN: The GDD does not decide this. It must never be invented; a row needing it escalates to human review.

rules.name: four_attacks_only
rules.requirement: The authored attack set is exactly A, B, C and D. No fifth attack, no alternate move set, and no per-phase-exclusive attack may appear.
rules.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 5 -- 'Four-attack course set'
rules.kb_anchor: vanguard-telegraphs.md :: The four authored attacks (no names in the GDD - this is the gap)

rules.name: readability_requirement
rules.requirement: Every attack must carry a readability requirement: a visible committed cue before the strike, and a deliberate punishable opening after it. Armor and scale may intensify presentation but must not remove readable counterplay.
rules.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 5 -- attack table 'Readability requirement' column, and 'Behavioral intent'
rules.kb_anchor: vanguard-telegraphs.md :: Behavioral intent (tone reference for telegraph/announcer copy)

rules.name: phase2_same_moveset
rules.requirement: Phase 2 re-times the same four authored attacks. It must never be described as a new move, a new move set, a transformation, or a per-phase-exclusive attack.
rules.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 6 -- 'Phase 2 escalation' ('Same four authored attacks - no transformation rig and no second move set')
rules.kb_anchor: vanguard-telegraphs.md :: Phase 2 escalation (same four attacks, re-timed - never a new moveset)

rules.name: no_runtime_ai
rules.requirement: Crimson Vanguard is deterministic authored gameplay AI. Generated text must not imply runtime learning, adaptation to the player, or any runtime AI-model call.
rules.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 5 -- 'REVISED - RUNTIME AI BOUNDARY'; reinforced in section 06, page 5

rules.name: scope_lock
rules.requirement: One player, one authored AI opponent, one arena, one shared combat framework, four authored attacks, one complete duel. Deferred content must never appear in a generated row.
rules.source: GDD v0.4 section 09, page 15 -- 'Course Scope Lock & Future Expansion'
rules.kb_anchor: core-canon.md :: Scope lock (do not exceed in generated content)

rules.name: no_invented_numbers
rules.requirement: The GDD states each attack's range and purpose qualitatively and marks every timing range provisional pending playtest. No generated free-text field may assert a numeric gameplay value -- damage, range in cm, cooldown, travel cap, or exact timing.
rules.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 5 -- attack table gives a qualitative 'Range / purpose' only; state-flow timings are labelled provisional. Open values enumerated in docs/unreal/ATTACK_DATA_SOURCE_AUDIT.md
rules.kb_anchor: vanguard-telegraphs.md :: The six-state loop (authored, deterministic - never LLM-driven)

rules.name: attack_d_no_snap
rules.requirement: Attack D is a short propulsion-assisted approach. It must state a thruster cue before movement, and must never describe a hidden or full-arena snap.
rules.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 5 -- attack D readability requirement, 'Thruster cue before movement; no hidden full-arena snap'
rules.kb_anchor: vanguard-telegraphs.md :: The four authored attacks (no names in the GDD - this is the gap)

A.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 5 -- 'Four-attack course set' table, row A

B.readability_requirement: Visible first beat and stable tracking limit
B.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 5 -- 'Four-attack course set' table, row B

C.readability_requirement: Clear body direction and visible active range
C.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 5 -- 'Four-attack course set' table, row C

D.readability_requirement: Thruster cue before movement; no hidden full-arena snap
D.source: GDD v0.4 section 04, page 5 -- 'Four-attack course set' table, row D
